newsitem.title: USA: CBOT CORN CLOSES LOWER ON MIDWEST RAINS, SOYBEANS.
newsitem.headline: CBOT CORN CLOSES LOWER ON MIDWEST RAINS, SOYBEANS.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on rains over the weekend in the U.S. Midwest and forecasts for more moisture, traders said.
A sharp drop in soybean futures also weighed on corn futures, they said.

"It (the market) did exactly what it should have done. The rain was bearish for beans and probably a little too late for corn," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man International "Corn is already pollinated and we may be able to get a little better test weight but it won't help the yields much."

The rainfall made a subtle penetration during the weekend into the dry corn growing region of the Midwest, especially in central Illinois, and additional crop-enhancing rainfall was expected over the next several days.
Weather Services Corp's Joel Burgio said corn plants in the driest areas of Illinois and Indiana received light weekend showers but more rain is forecast.
Corn closed near the day's highs on commercial short covering and positioning before Tuesday's USDA crop report.
Corn closed 1/4 to four cents lower, with September down 3-3/4 at $2.49-3/4.

Corn may have found some underpinning from USDA's weekly export inspections report that pegged corn export inspections at 36.487 million bushels, above expectations for 24 million to 28 million bushels.

Cargill Inc sold five million bushels of December, LIT America sold four million December, ABN Amro Chicago Corp sold 6.5 million December and Refco Inc sold four million December and bought three million December, traders said.
Farmers Commodities Corp spread two million bushels of September/December at four cents, premium December and Tenco Inc did one million December/March at 8-1/2 cents, premium March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 54,000 contracts, above the 50,206 traded Friday.

In corn options, Continental Grain bought 1,000 December $3.40 calls at 3/4 to 5/8 cent, ING Derivatives sold 1,000 September $2.50 puts at seven to 7-1/2 cents and Cargill Investor Services sold 800 December $2.30 calls at 23 to 23-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 24,083 traded Friday.
